now.note: Update by hand from bom.gov.au/climate/enso and bom.gov.au/climate/ahead/outlooks. Shown on the Rain tab.
now.headline: A near-record El Niño, but its grip on our rain loosens as summer arrives.

items.name: El Niño (Pacific Ocean)
items.what: One of the strongest on record: the central Pacific is about 2.7 °C warmer than normal. It should peak in December or January and last into autumn 2027. El Niño mostly dries our winter and spring; its hold on summer rain is weak.

items.name: Indian Ocean Dipole
items.what: Cool water off north-west Australia has cut the moisture that feeds our winter and spring rain. It is weakening (index +0.53 °C) and should be neutral by early summer, so it matters little for the season ahead.

items.name: Southern Annular Mode
items.what: The westerly winds sat further south through November. In summer that can push moist easterlies onto south-east Australia and add showers. It is expected to drift back to neutral.

items.name: Sea temperatures
items.what: Waters off southern Australia have been up to 3 °C warmer than normal. Warm seas add moisture, so when storms do come they can drop more rain.

items.name: Bureau 3-month outlook, Dec–Feb
items.what: For southern South Australia there is no clear signal: above- and below-average rain are about equally likely. Summer is our driest season anyway.
